goal: Complete the #479 remainders on StripeLocationsReconcilePoller: add a composite partial index for the reconcile accounts query, persist the keyset resume cursor across worker restarts, and emit a sustained-truncation alert when the cycle deadline keeps aborting the sweep.
non_goals: Do NOT auto-correct drift (poller stays detect-and-alert only).
Do NOT change ACCOUNT_FAN_OUT_CONCURRENCY, ACCOUNT_TIMEOUT_MS, CYCLE_TIMEOUT_MS, or INITIAL_RUN_DELAY_MS.
Do NOT change which subscription statuses are reconciled (active/past_due/trialing).
Do NOT build a generic poller-cursor framework — poller_cursors is a real table but this poller is its only writer for now (no abstraction before a 2nd use).
Do NOT add a Discord/queue-health routing rule (the residual feature:stripe_reconciliation routing gap noted in drift-alert.ts stays out of scope).
Do NOT change the in-memory cursor + bounded fan-out already shipped in #487 — only add durability + the alert underneath them.
user_visible_behavior: Ops-observable: after a worker restart the reconcile rotation RESUMES from the persisted cursor instead of restarting from the top of the account list.

Ops-observable: when the cycle deadline truncates the sweep for 3 consecutive cycles (no full drain in between), a warning-level Sentry alert fires (tag feature:stripe_reconciliation, structured-log fallback when SENTRY_DSN unset).
Ops-observable: a single truncated cycle still self-heals via the cursor next cycle and stays log-only (designed behavior, not an alert).
invariants: Tenant isolation: poller_cursors holds no tenant data (poller_name + uuid + updated_at); reconcile query scoping is unchanged.
Invariant #15: cursor-store is a worker helper taking sql as an explicit parameter; only the poller (a composition root registered in worker/index.ts) imports the singleton and passes it down.
Invariant #3 backstop: the single-flight guard + cycle deadline still release inProgress on every path; persistence must not introduce a path that holds inProgress or blocks a tick.
Cursor correctness: persisted value equals the in-memory working copy at all times (one owner of the cursor value); rotation-complete persists null.
Boot ordering: the first runOnce must not read the cursor before the boot load resolves (INITIAL_RUN_DELAY_MS gives 45s of slack, but the read is gated on the load promise regardless).
edge_cases: poller_cursors row absent on first-ever boot -> treat as null (start from top).
poller_cursors read fails at boot -> log and start from null (safe: a from-top rotation is always correct); do not crash the poller.

Cursor upsert fails mid-cycle -> log-and-swallow (best-effort after the primary side effect, per the crash-net rule); in-memory cursor still advances so the running process stays correct; next successful upsert re-persists.
Single truncation then full drain next cycle -> counter resets, no alert.
Rotation completes (cursor -> null) across multiple cycles -> counts as a drain, resets the truncation counter.
Empty account list (accounts.length === 0) -> drain state, resets the truncation counter, persists null.

Truncation is defined as dispatched < accounts.length. An abort with dispatched === 0 (fully stalled, e.g. parked on pool acquisition then deadline) DOES count as a truncation for the counter — a cycle that made zero progress is exactly the sustained-truncation signal; the cursor is left untouched in that case (nothing was claimed).
